claim: Intravital microscopy (IVM) enables live imaging of animals at single-cell level, offering essential insights into cancer progression.
source: Intravital microscopy (IVM) enables live imaging of animals at single-cell level, offering essential insights into cancer progression.
evidence: This is a general statement about IVM capabilities that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: IVM allows for the observation of single-cell behaviors within their natural 3D tissue environments.
source: This technique allows for the observation of single-cell behaviors within their natural 3D tissue environments, shedding light on how genetic and microenvironmental changes influence the complex dynamics of tumors.
evidence: This statement describes the technical capability of IVM based on established knowledge of the technique.

claim: Traditional uni-parametric approaches can neglect single-cell heterogeneous in vivo behavior and limit insights into microenvironmental influences on cellular behavior.
source: IVM generates highly complex datasets that often exceed the analytical capacity of traditional uni-parametric approaches, which can neglect single-cell heterogeneous in vivo behavior and limit insights into microenvironmental influences on cellular behavior.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of existing methods based on inference from the limitations observed in the field.

claim: BEHAV3D Tumor Profiler (BEHAV3D-TP) is a computational framework that enables unbiased single-cell classification based on morphological, environmental, and dynamic single-cell features.
source: To overcome these limitations, we present BEHAV3D Tumor Profiler (BEHAV3D-TP), a computational framework that enables unbiased single-cell classification based on a range of morphological, environmental, and dynamic single-cell features.
evidence: This describes the tool developed in this study, representing a primary finding.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP integrates with widely used 2D and 3D image processing pipelines.
source: BEHAV3D-TP integrates with widely used 2D and 3D image processing pipelines, enabling researchers without advanced computational expertise to profile cancer and healthy cell dynamics in IVM data from mouse models.
evidence: This is a technical capability of the tool demonstrated through its implementation and testing.

claim: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor characterized by invasive progression.
source: Here, we apply BEHAV3D-TP to study diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor characterized by invasive progression.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DMG characteristics in the medical literature.

claim: Distinct migratory behaviors of DMG cells are associated with specific TME components, including tumor-associated macrophages and vasculature.
source: By extending BEHAV3D-TP to incorporate tumor microenvironment (TME) data from IVM or fixed correlative imaging, we demonstrate that distinct migratory behaviors of DMG cells are associated with specific TME components, including tumor-associated macrophages and vasculature.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data and analysis.

claim: Tumors comprise many different cell populations that are in constant evolution.
source: Cancer is a complex disease driven by a sequence of genetic and microenvironmental changes. As a result, tumors comprise many different cell populations that are in constant evolution (Vitale et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Vitale et al., 2021.

claim: Tumor heterogeneity differentially promotes key characteristics of individual cancer cells, including proliferation, invasion, and drug resistance.
source: This tumor heterogeneity has important biological and clinical implications as it differentially promotes key characteristics of individual cancer cells, including proliferation, invasion, and drug resistance (Lawson et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lawson et al., 2018.

claim: Recent spatial transcriptomic and proteomic profiling provides evidence for the existence of multiple distinct microenvironmental niches within one tumor.
source: For example, recent spatial transcriptomic and proteomic profiling provides evidence for the existence of multiple distinct microenvironmental niches within one tumor (Elhanani et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Elhanani et al., 2023.

claim: Spatial transcriptomic and proteomic techniques can only provide static information and make use of thin tissue sections that are only one cell layer thick.
source: However, these techniques can only provide static information and make use of thin tissue sections that are only one cell layer thick.
evidence: This is a known limitation of these techniques based on established knowledge of the methods.

claim: IVM has provided many new insights into the dynamics of tumor heterogeneity and the development of therapy resistance.
source: Over the past years, it has provided many new insights into the dynamics of tumor heterogeneity and the development of therapy resistance (Scheele et al., 2016; Entenberg et al., 2023; Alieva et al., 2014; Alieva et al., 2019; Alieva and Rios, 2019; Zomer et al., 2022; Alieva et al., 2017; Janssen et al., 2013; Croci et al., 2023; Zomer et al., 2013; Zomer et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations documenting IVM applications.

claim: Only a small portion of tumor cells is motile in mouse breast cancer models.
source: For example, intravital imaging of mouse breast cancer models revealed that only a small portion of tumor cells is motile (Chen et al., 2019)
evidence: This finding is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2019.

claim: Fast- and slow-migrating cells are present in distinct regions of the tumor.
source: and that fast- and slow-migrating cells are present in distinct regions of the tumor (Alieva et al., 2019, Bayarmagnai et al., 2018).
evidence: This finding is supported by citations to Alieva et al., 2019 and Bayarmagnai et al., 2018.

claim: Additional heterogeneity exists among migrating tumor cells that can move randomly or directionally relative to other tumor cells and/or surrounding healthy tissue.
source: Moreover, additional heterogeneity exists among migrating tumor cells that can, for instance, move randomly or directionally relative to other tumor cells and/or surrounding healthy tissue (Alieva et al., 2019).
evidence: This finding is supported by a citation to Alieva et al., 2019.

claim: Traditional IVM analyses have considered cancer cells or the tumor microenvironment (TME) as a homogeneous population, thereby ignoring heterogeneity at the single-cell level.
source: However, traditional IVM analyses have considered cancer cells or the tumor microenvironment (TME) as a homogeneous population, thereby ignoring heterogeneity at the single-cell level and the influence of the local microenvironment, where interactions between neighboring cells may affect cellular behavior.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of traditional methods based on inference from the literature.

claim: Recent studies have used unbiased approaches using morpho-kinetic parameters derived from live imaging to classify cells and explore the single-cell behavioral landscape.
source: To address these complexities, recent studies have used unbiased approaches using morpho-kinetic parameters derived from live in vitro (Shannon et al., 2024) or in vivo imaging to classify cells and explore the single-cell behavioral landscape as an additional omic layer (Crainiciuc et al., 2022; Dekkers et al., 2023; Freckmann et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to recent studies.

claim: BEHAV3D was previously developed to perform behavioral phenotyping of engineered T cells targeting cancer.
source: In line with this concept of characterizing cellular dynamic properties for cell classification, we have previously developed an analytical platform termed BEHAV3D (Dekkers et al., 2023, Alieva et al., 2024) allowing us to perform behavioral phenotyping of engineered T cells targeting cancer.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: BEHAV3D was initially developed to analyze T cell migratory behavior under controlled in vitro conditions.
source: While BEHAV3D was initially developed to analyze T cell migratory behavior under controlled in vitro conditions, we sought to expand its application to investigate tumor cell behaviors in IVM data, where the complexity of the TME presents distinct analytical challenges.
evidence: This describes the original scope of BEHAV3D based on previous work.

claim: Significant efforts have been made to develop open-source segmentation and tracking tools for live imaging data, including IVM.
source: While significant efforts have been made to develop open-source segmentation and tracking tools for live imaging data, including IVM (Pizzagalli et al., 2018; Pizzagalli et al., 2022; Joseph et al., 2020; Molina-Moreno et al., 2022; Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al., 2024; Ershov et al., 2022)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to tool development papers.

claim: Fewer tools exist for the unbiased analysis of tumor dynamics compared to segmentation and tracking tools.
source: fewer tools exist for the unbiased analysis of tumor dynamics.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gap in the literature identified by the authors.

claim: Implementing analytical methods for tumor dynamics often requires substantial computational expertise, limiting accessibility for many biomedical researchers.
source: One major barrier is that implementing such analytical methods often requires substantial computational expertise, limiting accessibility for many biomedical researchers conducting IVM experiments.
evidence: This is an inference about barriers in the field based on the authors' experience and observations.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP expands the capabilities of BEHAV3D by incorporating key features designed for in vivo tumor cell dynamics.
source: BEHAV3D-TP expands the capabilities of BEHAV3D by incorporating key features designed for in vivo tumor cell dynamics (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the advancement made in this study, supported by Figure 1 showing the pipeline.

claim: The BEHAV3D-TP pipeline includes extensions that integrate tumor cell behavior with spatial features within the native TME.
source: The pipeline includes extensions that integrate tumor cell behavior with spatial features within the native TME, using either in situ (IVM) or fixed correlative imaging to reveal how distinct spatial niches influence tumor dynamics.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the tool developed in this study.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP supports both commercial and open-source data formats.
source: To further facilitate unbiased analysis of tumor dynamics, we developed BEHAV3D-TP as a flexible tool that supports both commercial and open-source data formats, ensuring broad compatibility across different research workflows.
evidence: This describes a technical feature of the tool implemented in this study.

claim: The BEHAV3D-TP pipeline supports 2D and 3D data formats generated by Imaris and by Fiji plugins such as TrackMate, MTrackJ, and ManualTracking.
source: The pipeline supports 2D and 3D data formats generated by Imaris and by Fiji plugins such as TrackMate, MTrackJ, and ManualTracking, enabling processing of datasets from the most widely used segmentation and tracking solutions.
evidence: This describes the compatibility features of the tool implemented in this study.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP was applied to a range of published tumor and healthy tissue IVM datasets to demonstrate its versatility and broad applicability.
source: We demonstrate the versatility and broad applicability of BEHAV3D-TP by applying it to a range of published tumor and healthy tissue IVM datasets.
evidence: This describes the validation approach used in the study.

claim: DMG has the capacity to spread to other regions of the brain and the spinal cord.
source: Next, we focused on Diffuse Midline Glioma (DMG), a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor characterized by invasive growth and its capacity to spread to other regions of the brain and the spinal cord (Buczkowicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Buczkowicz et al., 2014.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP was designed as a modular Jupyter Notebook featuring an intuitive graphical user interface (GUI).
source: To enhance accessibility and encourage widespread adoption among researchers studying single tumor cell dynamics in live imaging and inspired by previous work on democratizing advanced image analysis (Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al., 2024; Gómez-de-Mariscal et al., 2023; Von Chamier et al., 2021), we designed BEHAV3D-TP as a modular Jupyter Notebook featuring an intuitive graphical user interface (GUI) (Figure 1 and Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This describes the design of the tool, supported by Figure 1 and video demonstration.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP runs directly in a web browser and requires only a Google account for access.
source: The platform runs directly in a web browser and requires only a Google account for access.
evidence: This describes the accessibility feature of the tool implemented in this study.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP implementation within the Google Colaboratory (Colab) framework ensures efficient cloud-based computation with free and scalable resources.
source: BEHAV3D-TP implementation within the Google Colaboratory (Colab) framework not only ensures efficient cloud-based computation with free and scalable resources but also enhances tool accessibility by eliminating the need for local software installation, a common barrier for inexperienced users.
evidence: This describes the technical implementation and its benefits.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP eliminates the need for local software installation, a common barrier for inexperienced users.
source: BEHAV3D-TP implementation within the Google Colaboratory (Colab) framework not only ensures efficient cloud-based computation with free and scalable resources but also enhances tool accessibility by eliminating the need for local software installation, a common barrier for inexperienced users.
evidence: This describes a design feature intended to improve accessibility, based on inference about user barriers.

claim: The heterogeneity module of BEHAV3D-TP enables researchers to uncover diverse patterns of tumor morphodynamic behavior.
source: After time-lapse image file processing and preparation using various frameworks (Figure 1a), the central component of BEHAV3D-TP — called the heterogeneity module (Figure 1b) — enables researchers to uncover diverse patterns of tumor morphodynamic behavior.
evidence: This describes the function of a key module, supported by Figure 1.

claim: The large-scale phenotyping module uses post-IVM fixed imaging data for tissue phenotyping.
source: The large-scale phenotyping module uses post-IVM fixed imaging data for tissue phenotyping, identifying extensive regions with specific TME characteristics, and assessing the distribution of distinct tumor cell behavioral patterns within these regions.
evidence: This describes the function of the large-scale phenotyping module.

claim: The small-scale phenotyping module uses in situ-labeled TME structures from IVM data.
source: The small-scale phenotyping module uses in situ-labeled TME structures from IVM data, facilitating the correlation of these TME features within the microenvironment of individual tumor cell neighborhoods.
evidence: This describes the function of the small-scale phenotyping module.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP analyzed multivariate similarities in morphological and dynamic features using the dynamic time warping algorithm.
source: The datasets, processed with different segmentation and tracking tools, were analyzed for multivariate similarities in morphological and dynamic features (summarized in Table 1) using the dynamic time warping algorithm (Alieva et al., 2024).
evidence: This describes the analytical method used, supported by a citation.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP provided a more granular characterization of breast cancer cell behaviors, uncovering additional migratory patterns not reported in the original study.
source: BEHAV3D-TP provided a more granular characterization of these behaviors, uncovering additional migratory patterns not reported in the original study (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–c).
evidence: This is a finding from applying BEHAV3D-TP to published data, supported by supplementary figures.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP identified behaviors such as Fast, Intermediate, Very slow, and Static in breast cancer cell lines that had a different distribution among both tumor cell lines.
source: Specifically, we identified behaviors such as Fast, Intermediate, Very slow, and Static that had a different distribution among both tumor cell lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d–e).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis, supported by supplementary figures.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP confirmed the compatibility with advanced segmentation frameworks including Cellpose 2.0 within the MaSCOT-AI workflow.
source: This workflow not only confirmed the compatibility of BEHAV3D-TP with advanced segmentation frameworks but also its usage to unravel distinct morphodynamic patterns in non-tumor epithelial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b and c).
evidence: This describes a validation of tool compatibility demonstrated in the study.

claim: HR +TEB exhibit greater migratory capacity than HR- TEB.
source: Consistent with previous findings that HR +TEB (Pr-cre/Confetti) exhibit greater migratory capacity than HR- TEB (Elf5-rtTA/TetO-Cre/Confetti)
evidence: This references a previous finding that is being confirmed in this analysis.

claim: The difference in migratory capacity between HR +TEB and HR- TEB is primarily driven by a distinct morphodynamic behavior characterized by a rounder shape and increased motility.
source: our analysis suggests that this difference is primarily driven by a distinct morphodynamic behavior (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d). Specifically, HR +TEB more frequently exhibited characteristics of Cluster 2, defined by a rounder shape and increased motility.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis, supported by supplementary figures.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP's ability to uncover complex, multiparametric cellular behaviors is often missed in analyses focused on single-value comparisons across conditions.
source: Despite the small sample size requiring further validation, these results demonstrate BEHAV3D-TP's ability to uncover complex, multiparametric cellular behaviors that are often missed in analyses focused on single-value comparisons across conditions.
evidence: This is an inference about the tool's capabilities based on the results obtained.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP identified distinct GBM morphodynamic patterns, each characterized by unique combinations of morphological and dynamic features and associated with specific spatial distributions.
source: BEHAV3D-TP identified distinct GBM morphodynamic patterns, each characterized by unique combinations of morphological and dynamic features and associated with specific spatial distributions (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b–d).
evidence: This is a finding from applying BEHAV3D-TP to GBM data, supported by supplementary figures.

claim: Cluster 1 GBM cells (large and slow-moving) were more isolated and located farther from neighboring cells compared to Cluster 6 (small, fast, persistent cells) and Cluster 4 (very small, static cells).
source: Cluster 1, consisting of large and slow-moving cells, was more isolated and located farther from neighboring cells compared to Cluster 6 (small, fast, persistent cells) and Cluster 4 (very small, static cells).
evidence: This is a finding from the spatial analysis of GBM clusters.

claim: The compact spatial arrangement of small cells within the tumor may contribute to their reduced size.
source: These findings suggest that the compact spatial arrangement of small cells within the tumor may contribute to their reduced size.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the spatial distribution findings.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP is versatile and broadly applicable across diverse biological systems, dimensionalities (2D and 3D), imaging modalities, and data processing pipelines.
source: Collectively, these findings underscore the versatility and broad applicability of BEHAV3D-TP across diverse biological systems, dimensionalities (2D and 3D), imaging modalities, and data processing pipelines, supporting its utility as a robust tool for the in-depth analysis of cellular behavioral patterns in IVM data.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multiple validation experiments performed.

claim: The BEHAV3D-TP heterogeneity module identified 7 DMG behavioral clusters: retreating, slow retreating, erratic, static, slow, slow invading, and invading.
source: The BEHAV3D-TP heterogeneity module identified 7 DMG behavioral clusters: retreating, slow retreating, erratic, static, slow, slow invading, and invading (Figure 2b–d, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from applying BEHAV3D-TP to DMG data, supported by Figure 2 and video.

claim: Invading and retreating DMG clusters are characterized by fast movement away from and towards the tumor edge, respectively.
source: Of particular interest were cells from the invading and retreating clusters, characterized by fast movement away from and towards the tumor edge, respectively (Figure 2c-f, Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of specific clusters identified in the analysis, supported by figures.

claim: Approximately 10% of DMG cancer cells were displaying invasive behavior in this particular DMG model.
source: In fact, in this particular DMG model, approximately 10% of the cancer cells were displaying invasive behavior (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis, supported by a supplementary figure.

claim: About 10% of DMG cells were moving back to the tumor edge (retreating, slow retreating clusters).
source: Interestingly, about another 10% of DMG cells were moving back to the tumor edge (retreating, slow retreating clusters; Figure 2—figure supplement 1d)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis, supported by a supplementary figure.

claim: Retreating behavior has been previously observed for glioblastoma and suggested to be regulated by differential chemotactic signaling by the tumor edge and the surrounding brain parenchyma.
source: behavior that has been previously observed for glioblastoma and suggested to be regulated by differential chemotactic signaling by the tumor edge and the surrounding brain parenchyma (Alieva et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Erratic DMG cells display fast non-directed migration behavior.
source: We also observed erratic cells that display fast non-directed migration behavior and static cells that are non-migratory (Figure 2c–f).
evidence: This describes a behavioral cluster identified in the analysis, supported by Figure 2.

claim: Static DMG cells are non-migratory.
source: We also observed erratic cells that display fast non-directed migration behavior and static cells that are non-migratory (Figure 2c–f).
evidence: This describes a behavioral cluster identified in the analysis, supported by Figure 2.

claim: The distinct behavioral patterns were detected in all intravitally imaged mice.
source: Crucially, the distinct behavioral patterns were detected in all intravitally imaged mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d), ruling out any sample bias that might lead to clusters consisting solely of cells from a single tumor or mouse.
evidence: This is a finding that validates the reproducibility of the results across samples.

claim: CytoMAP spatial phenotyping analysis identified three different environmental niches: Void regions, TAMM/oligo regions, and TAMM/vascularized regions.
source: Subsequent CytoMAP (Winkler et al., 2009) spatial phenotyping analysis identified three different environmental niches: Void regions (less vascularized and with low glial infiltration), TAMM/oligo regions (enriched in oligodendrocytes, TAMM, and tumor cells), and TAMM/vascularized regions (highly vascularized regions enriched in TAMM; Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-c).
evidence: This is a finding from the spatial phenotyping analysis, supported by Figure 3 and supplementary figures.

claim: Void regions are less vascularized and with low glial infiltration.
source: Void regions (less vascularized and with low glial infiltration)
evidence: This describes the characteristics of a TME niche identified in the analysis.

claim: TAMM/oligo regions are enriched in oligodendrocytes, TAMM, and tumor cells.
source: TAMM/oligo regions (enriched in oligodendrocytes, TAMM, and tumor cells)
evidence: This describes the characteristics of a TME niche identified in the analysis.

claim: TAMM/vascularized regions are highly vascularized regions enriched in TAMM.
source: TAMM/vascularized regions (highly vascularized regions enriched in TAMM; Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-c).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of a TME niche identified in the analysis, supported by figures.

claim: Invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions.
source: Interestingly, invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions that contain a higher proportion of static cells
evidence: This is a finding from comparing behavioral clusters across TME niches.

claim: Void regions contain a higher proportion of static cells compared to TAMM/vascularized regions.
source: invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions that contain a higher proportion of static cells
evidence: This is a finding from comparing behavioral clusters across TME niches.

claim: TAMM/Oligo microenvironments contain more slow retreating cells compared to the other regions.
source: and TAMM/Oligo microenvironments contain more slow retreating cells compared to the other regions (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing behavioral clusters across TME niches, supported by figures.

claim: Single parameters showed a restricted ability to identify differences in cellular behavior among various environments compared to multiparametric behavioral mapping.
source: Interestingly, single parameters showed a restricted ability to identify differences in cellular behavior among various environments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1e–g), underscoring the importance of multiparametric behavioral mapping in revealing more nuanced cellular behavior that cannot be captured solely by individual dynamic parameters.
evidence: This is a comparative finding demonstrating the advantage of the multiparametric approach, supported by supplementary figures.

claim: Invading DMG cells tended to be more sparsely distributed relative to neighboring DMG cells compared to static cells.
source: Compared to static cells, invading cells tended to be more sparsely distributed relative to neighboring DMG cells (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c)
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale phenotyping analysis, supported by figures.

claim: Invading DMG cells were found to reside in regions enriched with TAMMs.
source: In agreement with our large-scale TME phenotyping results (Figure 3), invading DMG cells were found to reside in regions enriched with TAMMs (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale phenotyping analysis, supported by Figure 4.

claim: A higher proportion of invading cells were in close proximity to TAMMs compared to static, retreating, and slow-retreating clusters.
source: Specifically, a higher proportion of invading cells were in close proximity to TAMMs compared to static, retreating, and slow-retreating clusters (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the proximity analysis, supported by Figure 4.

claim: Invading DMG cells frequently migrated directionally toward TAMMs.
source: They frequently migrated directionally toward TAMMs (Figure 4d, Figure 4—video 1)
evidence: This is a finding from the directional migration analysis, supported by Figure 4 and video.

claim: Migration of invading DMG cells is at least partially mediated by chemotaxis toward TAMMs.
source: suggesting that migration of this behavioral cluster is at least partially mediated by chemotaxis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the directional migration findings.

claim: All fast-migrating behavioral clusters (invading, erratic, and retreating) were found to be generally closer to blood vessels.
source: Furthermore, all fast-migrating behavioral clusters (invading, erratic, and retreating) were found to be generally closer to blood vessels (Figure 4b and e)
evidence: This is a finding from the proximity analysis, supported by Figure 4.

claim: Perivascular invasion is a more efficient movement route for fast-migrating DMG cells.
source: suggesting that perivascular invasion is a more efficient movement route for these cells (Figure 4f)
evidence: This is an inference based on the proximity findings, supported by Figure 4.

claim: Perivascular migration has been previously observed for adult glioblastoma cells.
source: a mode of migration that has been previously observed for adult glioblastoma cells as well (Alieva et al., 2019; Wallmann et al., 2018; Ravin et al., 2023; Gupta et al., 2024; Nimmerjahn et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Slow-retreating DMG cells were found in regions enriched for SR101+ cells.
source: Lastly, particularly slow-retreating DMG cells were found in regions enriched for SR101+ cells (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d)
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale phenotyping analysis, supported by figures.

claim: SR101+ enrichment near slow-retreating DMG cells may reflect oligodendrocyte-like (OC-like) tumor DMG cells that have been found near oligodendrocytes.
source: perhaps reflecting oligodendrocyte-like (OC-like) tumor DMG cells that have been found near oligodendrocytes (Xin et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation to Xin et al., 2024.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP is an unbiased approach based on the integration of multiple parameters measured by IVM.
source: In contrast to traditional pipelines that rely on the analysis of single parameters such as cell speed or displacement (Venkataramani et al., 2022; Bera et al., 2022; Gertler and Condeelis, 2011) or that use an artificial threshold to assign a specific behavior to cells (Alieva et al., 2017), BEHAV3D-TP is an unbiased approach based on the integration of multiple parameters measured by IVM.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of BEHAV3D-TP in contrast to traditional methods.

claim: Using the heterogeneity module of BEHAV3D-TP, behavioral phenotypes were uncovered that have not been described before and that could not have been identified using single parameter analysis.
source: Using the heterogeneity module of our BEHAV3D-TP pipeline, we uncovered behavioral phenotypes that have not been described before and that could not have been identified using single parameter analysis.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of findings enabled by the tool.

claim: Invading and retreating clusters are composed of cells with a similar cell speed but with an opposite migration direction.
source: For example, our analysis revealed invading and retreating clusters, composed of cells with a similar cell speed but with an opposite migration direction, an important biological and clinical difference.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis that illustrates the value of multiparametric classification.

claim: Bidirectional migration is likely mediated by different chemotactic cues and by the composition of the local TME.
source: Likely, bidirectional migration is mediated by different chemotactic cues and by the composition of the local TME (Kluiver et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: Previous studies suggest a major role for the microenvironment in promoting tumor cell spread into the healthy brain.
source: Previous studies suggest a major role for the microenvironment in promoting tumor cell spread into the healthy brain (Taylor and Monje, 2022; Erices et al., 2023; Patel et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The small-scale TME analysis has a higher predictive value compared to the large-scale TME analysis.
source: Our results also show that the small-scale TME analysis has a higher predictive value compared to the large-scale TME analysis
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the two analytical approaches.

claim: A cell's direct microenvironment is a more important regulator of its behavior compared to its macroenvironment.
source: suggesting that a cell's direct microenvironment is a more important regulator of its behavior compared to its macroenvironment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparative predictive value of small-scale vs large-scale analysis.

claim: TAMMs and blood vessels were associated with specific behavioral phenotypes.
source: Indeed, we found that TAMMs and blood vessels were associated with specific behavioral phenotypes, showing the power of BEHAV3D-TP small-scale phenotyping module in identifying novel regulators of cellular behavior.
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale phenotyping analysis.

claim: Slow-retreating DMG cells were found in environments enriched for SR101+ cells, an observation that has not been made before.
source: This is exemplified by our finding that slow-retreating DMG cells were found in environments enriched for SR101+ cells, an observation that has not been made before.
evidence: This claims novelty for a specific finding from the analysis.

claim: Existing literature strongly supports the notion that cell dynamics can serve as a proxy for functional states and phenotypic heterogeneity.
source: While our current study does not provide direct functional validation of the distinct motility clusters identified, existing literature strongly supports the notion that cell dynamics can serve as a proxy for functional states and phenotypic heterogeneity.
evidence: This is a statement about existing knowledge in the field.

claim: Prior work has demonstrated that variations in cell motility patterns can reflect underlying functional characteristics.
source: Prior work, including studies by our group (Dekkers et al., 2023, Aragones et al., 2024) as well as (Crainiciuc et al., 2022) and (Freckmann et al., 2022), has demonstrated that variations in cell motility patterns can reflect underlying functional characteristics.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Cell morpho-dynamic features have been shown to correlate with differences in cell type identity, T-cell engagement, metastatic potential, and drug resistance states.
source: Specifically, cell morpho-dynamic features have been shown to correlate with differences in cell type identity, T-cell engagement, metastatic potential, and drug resistance states.
evidence: This is a statement about established correlations in the literature.

claim: Tumor cell behavior, as captured by BEHAV3D-TP, may serve as a predictive tool for deciphering functional tumor heterogeneity.
source: This growing body of evidence suggests that tumor cell behavior, as captured by BEHAV3D-TP, may serve as a predictive tool for deciphering functional tumor heterogeneity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential utility of the tool based on existing literature.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP allows for the selection of diverse feature types, supporting datasets that include both dynamic, morphological, spatial, and environmental parameters.
source: BEHAV3D-TP allows for the selection of diverse feature types, supporting datasets that include both dynamic, morphological, spatial, and environmental parameters.
evidence: This describes a capability of the tool.

claim: Expanding the feature set may introduce biologically irrelevant noise, particularly in 3D microscopy data where limited z-axis resolution can lead to morphological artifacts.
source: However, we recognize that expanding the feature set may introduce biologically irrelevant noise, particularly in 3D microscopy data where limited z-axis resolution can lead to morphological artifacts.
evidence: This is a cautionary statement based on knowledge of microscopy limitations.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP has been incorporated in a Google Colab notebook, allowing researchers with minimal programming skills to employ the tool online.
source: To enhance the accessibility of BEHAV3D-TP for researchers keen on studying tumor cell behavioral profiles through live imaging, we have incorporated our software in a Google Colab notebook, allowing researchers with minimal programming skills to employ the tool online without the requirement to install specific software environments nor the need to directly interact with the code.
